long_biography.plain_text:
Tinney began his career flying for a small helicopter and seaplane operator in Alaska. He recognised demand for glacier tours, bought a Bell 206 alongside his employer and helped assemble a three-aircraft operation. The partners then launched Air Center in the Caribbean, but the expansion failed. Tinney kept one helicopter and rebuilt with $3,600, flying tours from a remote part of an island golf course.

Hurricane Hugo pushed him to seek work less exposed to tourism cycles. He won his first United States Navy support contract in 1989 and developed Air Center around specialised government missions. After moving the operation to Fort Worth in 1997, he expanded its fleet and capabilities across shipboard logistics, rescue, medical evacuation and expeditionary airlift. He later led the acquisition and conversion of Airbus H225 helicopters for heavy utility work. Tinney remains a hands-on chief executive, check airman and flight-test pilot.
